edges.description: Overactive PKA phosphorylates GLI transcription factors, driving their repressor processing and switching off Hedgehog target genes.

Patient cells carrying a PRKACA variant show reduced primary ciliation; the primary cilium is the organelle on which Hedgehog signaling is transduced, so this is placed as a parallel consequence of the lesion rather than downstream of Hedgehog inhibition.
Loss of Hedgehog target-gene activation disrupts morphogen-dependent patterning in multiple developing tissues.
Impaired ciliary Hedgehog signal transduction contributes to the developmental patterning defect.
Failure of endocardial cushion fusion during cardiac development.
Hedgehog patterning controls anteroposterior limb/digit identity.
Impaired Hedgehog-dependent growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation.
Impaired growth-plate chondrocyte function reduces long-bone growth.
Ectodermal/epithelial-mesenchymal patterning defect in tooth development.
Ectodermal patterning defect in nail matrix.

nodes.description: PKA is a negative regulator of Hedgehog signaling: it phosphorylates GLI transcription factors (GLI3) to promote repressor processing. The CAFD1 variants keep PKA inappropriately active, so Hedgehog target-gene transcription is attenuated. Mutant PRKACA inhibited Hedgehog signaling in NIH 3T3 fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Heterozygous PRKACA variants (the recurrent missense p.Gly137Arg and an in-frame deletion p.Asn290_Ile292del) alter the PKA catalytic subunit alpha at surfaces that tether the regulatory subunits, weakening that interaction so the holoenzyme is more easily activated by cAMP. The net effect is raised PKA pathway activity; the gain comes from loss of regulatory-subunit restraint (ClinGen describes the mechanism as partial loss-of-function at the protein level, and the in-frame-deletion protein has lower intrinsic catalytic activity) rather than from higher intrinsic catalysis.

nodes.description: In-frame three-amino-acid deletion (c.870_878del) in the alpha-I helix substrate-tethering region; reduces type-II regulatory-subunit binding and overactivates PKA, with reduced patient-cell ciliation. Its phenotype differs from the recurrent missense allele — the single reported patient had PDA/PFO rather than AVSD or polydactyly, with skeletal dysplasia plus vasculopathy — so it is an expanded-spectrum allele.

Recurrent missense variant (c.409G>A), the archetypal CAFD1 allele, at a conserved regulatory-subunit tethering surface; gain-of-function. All classically reported CAFD1 patients to date carry this variant.
